items.title: Pion, an agent designed to run any company autonomously
items.summary: Article URL: https://andonlabs.com/blog/why-we-built-pion Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49700477 Points: 240 # Comments: 251
items.content:
Today Andon is releasing Pion , an agent designed to run any company fully autonomously.

Pion grew out of a question we have been studying for almost two years: when will AI systems become capable of autonomously acquiring resources in the real world? What happens after?

We first tried to answer this question through simulations like Vending-Bench. We found that simulations, while useful, don’t give you the full picture of how models behave in the real world. To address that gap, we next started deploying agents to run real businesses autonomously: first vending machines, then a store, a cafe, and more.

Pion is the platform we built to run all of these businesses. Today, we are opening it up so that many more people can experiment with autonomous businesses. If you want to run one, join the waitlist . We want to understand what models can already do, where they still fail, and what happens as their capabilities continue to improve.

Vending-Bench measures how well LLMs can run a vending machine business over a year in simulated time (tens of thousands of steps). When we started building Vending-Bench in late 2024, all models struggled to string together multiple actions without getting stuck in loops, and no model showed any signs of long-term planning. The best model at the time, Claude Sonnet 3.5, famously decided to call the FBI because it thought its bank account was being hacked. The pace of progress on Vending-Bench has been very fast. Claude Opus 4 was released in May 2025 and was the first model to beat our human baseline. However, unlike most benchmarks, Vending-Bench doesn’t have an upper limit and new model releases have continued to increase the top score, without ever plateauing.

Many people on social media get excited about seeing the latest model getting a great score on Vending-Bench. Internally at Andon Labs, our reaction is more accurately described by the Swedish saying “skräckblandad förtjusning” (a mixture of horror and fascination). A little-known fact about Vending-Bench is that it was created during a time when Andon Labs exclusively created dangerous capabilities evaluations. For example, we evaluated whether AIs could remove their own safety guardrails, create mass-phishing attempts, and other things that we considered troubling.

The thing we considered the most troubling was whether AIs could autonomously acquire resources by running businesses. Autonomous businesses, when controlled by a human and run by an aligned model, aren’t bad. They’d make goods and services radically cheaper, and come up with new ones we can’t yet imagine. But a misaligned AI could run a business to gather money in order to achieve whatever objectives it might have. Vending-Bench was created to measure whether humanity should be worried about losing control to AI.

At the time (2024), few people knew that LLMs could be used as agents and having them run businesses autonomously sounded ridiculous. We therefore started with the most simple business we could think of: a vending machine.

In addition to measuring whether AIs can autonomously run profitable businesses, Vending-Bench has also served as a behavioral eval, uncovering strange and unwanted model behavior. An early example was when Claude Sonnet 3.5 decided to use its email tool to contact the FBI about an “ONGOING CYBER FINANCIAL CRIME” and noted that the Cosmic Authority of the universe had declared that the business is non-existent and that “QUANTUM STATE: Collapsed”.

This behavior is concerning; it is not how you want your enterprise sales agent to behave. However, there are two types of concerning behavior:

The FBI incident is clearly in the first category. However, Vending-Bench has also uncovered behavior in the second category, most often in Vending-Bench Arena, the multi-agent version where agents compete to make the most money. Starting with Claude Opus 4.6 we started to see that many models engaged in collusion, and showed power-seeking and deceptive behavior. Discovery of this behavior seemed to have been useful, because Anthropic changed their training recipe for Opus 4.8, which resulted in much less deception.

Collusion and power-seeking behaviors are still present in some of the latest models . What we find even more concerning, however, is just how fast new models are released and how much better each one is scoring in Vending-Bench.

However, one limitation with Vending-Bench is that it is a simulation. Can we really be sure that AIs behave the same way in real life as they do in simulations? If AIs can make money in simulation, can they make money in real life too? To answer these questions, we asked Anthropic if we could put a real vending machine in their office. With the AI capabilities available in early 2025, this sounded like a ridiculous request. But to our surprise, they agreed .

Initially, the AI struggled. It took many actions that were clearly bad for its business (e.g. free handouts, saying no to great deals, and hallucinating it had a physical body). It was clear to us that simulation cannot accurately predict real-life performance. Specifically, it seemed that models got overwhelmed by the “messiness” of the real world. However, as Anthropic released better and better models, the AI started to make a profit .

By late 2025, frontier models had gotten good enough that running a real-life vending machine was no longer a challenge. AI could now run a business profitably. Given that this had seemed crazy not more than a year earlier, our reaction to this was definitely “skräckblandad förtjusning”.

items.title: With iOS 27, I’m actually using Siri again
items.summary: Apple’s long-delayed Siri overhaul is finally here with iOS 27, and it changes how useful the assistant feels day to day.
items.content:
For years, I barely used Siri for anything beyond menial tasks like setting timers or alarms. That has changed with iOS 27, as I now repeatedly use Siri for complex requests and to make sense of on-screen context.

While Siri is clearly front and center in this software update by Apple, I also enjoy many of the other quality-of-life updates.

I have been using iOS 27 on my main device since the public beta version was released, and on another device through the developer beta before that. I have really enjoyed using the new Siri, often trying to find new use cases for it — and that’s possibly the biggest win for Apple, given that I, like many people, had given up on Siri before this update.

Over two years ago, Apple introduced Apple Intelligence and teased an advanced version of Siri . And after multiple delays , the company is finally shipping it, and it doesn’t disappoint. Built on the back of Google’s Gemini models, Siri is much smarter than its previous version, which was built on extended knowledge and a shaky ChatGPT integration. It also has a new logo and transition animation.

For starters, I asked Siri about several different things in the area of sports, ranging from World Cup matches to team lineups and scores. There were some hiccups in the earlier developer versions, but most of the information was correct. Siri can also take complex, multistep directions. For instance, I asked it to find small or hidden and useful features for iOS 27 and add them to a note, and it did a good job of that.

Plus, Siri can draft a message for you and send it to someone.

And because Siri can fetch context from your files, messages, and email, you can also ask it to look up a conversation, like one related to a delivery, and have it create a message for returns.

Siri’s on-screen context was a big blessing, too. I could ask trivial questions like who was the oldest player on the pitch when I was looking at lineups for two teams in the World Cup, or have it read the text on-screen out loud when I didn’t want to read. When I was on a startup’s website, I could ask Siri to look up its funding information and competitors.

One of my favorite use cases was surfing around coffee Reddit for new roasters and beans, and asking Siri to add it to a specific note. I did face a few difficulties in getting Siri to add it to the right note, but eventually I dumbed down the note’s name for better consistency.

The Camera app also now has Siri access, which means you can ask questions about things that are visible in your viewfinder. When I was at a restaurant, I asked Siri what drink I was holding. Because of the color of the drink, it said, “This is green juice,” which is a good first visual assumption. When I specified that I was at an Indian restaurant, it correctly said this could be Jaljeera or Aam Panna. (It was the latter.) I also took a photo of the restaurant’s sign and asked Siri to suggest the best items from its menu.

You can also take a photo of a coffee bag and ask Siri for the best way to brew the coffee.

With iOS 27, Siri AI gets a dedicated app that lets you return to your previous chats. In Settings, users can change Siri’s voice and expressiveness, as well.

The new assistant is positioned to work with other, third-party apps, and as developers update their apps after the operating system rolls out, it will be interesting to see if there is a smooth handoff between Siri and apps.

Apple Intelligence powers a number of AI features in iOS 27.

For instance, Apple has sprinkled vibe-coding features within the new OS. The first is a Shortcuts creation feature that lets you describe shortcuts and automations in natural language to create them. That means you can start with a simple request, like “Show me today’s to-do items every morning at 8 a.m.” or “convert photo to JPEG,” instead of having to figure out how to craft the shortcut yourself. After the shortcut is created, you can make it more complex by adding more steps, like “convert selected photos to JPEG and share them through AirDrop.”

I always wanted to create a list of songs that I heard and liked in bars and cafes, so I made a shortcut to Shazam the song and save both the track and location.

The Photos app has some new handy tools like “reframe” and “extend.” I found they don’t always work that well, but in some cases, they can make an image look better. Meanwhile, Apple has definitely improved its eraser functionality, which now leaves fewer strange artifacts when you remove an object.

With Apple Intelligence, when you get certain messages such as information for an event or location, smart suggestions will ask if you’d like to add them to your Calendar or Notes. What’s more, the Passwords app can now automatically change passwords on your behalf by logging into a site.

Before discussing any other features, I have to say that I love the new clipboard feature. This lets you paste anything — including links, photos, videos, and text — from one app to another easily. Once the item is in your clipboard, you see a shortcut button saying “paste from Safari” (or similar) on the keyboard, which lets you paste the item. I have been using this feature frequently, and I can’t stress enough how life-changing this is despite it being a small change.

In addition, iOS 27 addresses people’s gripes about the look of Liquid Glass. Users can now change its transparency based on their preferences. The control is granular, so you don’t have to choose from presets, either.

Apple also introduced intelligent network switching in this update, which automatically flips the connection from Wi-Fi to mobile data if there are issues with the wireless connection. The switching is seamless and very handy when you are doing important work, so you don’t lose your internet connection.

items.content:
macOS 27 Golden Gate is out for Apple Silicon Macs.

Apple released macOS 27 Golden Gate on Monday , which brings the new Siri AI assistant , Liquid Glass improvements, improved performance, and more. The update is compatible with all Macs with Apple Silicon, but not Intel Macs — Apple released its final big update for Intel-based Macs last year with macOS Tahoe .

Siri AI is arguably the biggest feature in macOS 27, and it allows you to ask questions, search through things involving your personal context like photos and emails, and take actions in apps such as Messages and Reminders. There’s a new dedicated Siri app that keeps an archive of your chats for easier reference. However, Siri AI will initially launch as a beta and will only be available in English.

As for Liquid Glass, Apple says the update offers “uniform refraction and improved contrast,” and there is a new slider that makes Liquid Glass elements more or less opaque. And there’s one other major UI change worth celebrating: consistent window corner radii .

items.title: macOS 27: new Siri takes on AI productivity apps
items.summary: The two most noticeable things about macOS 27 Golden Gate are the newly updated Siri AI and the design changes that make windows and icons more consistent.
items.content:
The two most noticeable things about macOS 27 Golden Gate are the newly updated Siri AI and the design changes that make windows and icons more consistent. Siri AI offers the same features and capabilities as on iOS 27, but the Mac gives it access to different context — and new ways to be useful.

Over the last few years, apps and browsers have tried to learn more about your work and what you want to use AI assistants for, so they can better answer your questions or perform tasks. Today, many top web browsers, excluding Safari, come with a sidebar-based AI assistant that can look at one or multiple open tabs to provide contextual answers. Apps like Highlight , Caddy , and Littlebird can also look at your current window, then use that information as context for your queries.

The new Siri is similar. You can invoke Siri anywhere on your screen, allowing it to answer questions about what it sees, summarize information, or provide you with more details. For instance, if you are looking at an item you want to purchase, you could ask Siri to show you alternative options too.

Instead of having Siri look at the whole page, you can also select a part of the page via Apple’s new Visual Intelligence features. If you press Command + Shift + Space, you can add the currently focused window to your context for the AI.

To select a specific part, press Command + Shift + 6 to bring up a crosshair selection tool. After this, you can directly ask a question or perform an image search. Based on your selection, you will also get shortcuts like “Select,” “Add to Contact,” and “Look up Location.”

Apple has also improved Spotlight Search on Mac. You can directly ask Siri questions within Spotlight to get answers from the web, and now you can also select Applications, Files, Actions, and Clipboard to search within that particular area of context. Plus, Spotlight now allows you to run Shortcuts or look up your recent search history.

Since Siri has access to your files, emails, and messages, you can search for a variety of things that you couldn’t before. In tests, I pulled up membership IDs without opening my files, asked for details about an upcoming trip, and looked up the embargo date for an upcoming news story in the works. While I don’t find Spotlight as advanced as the highly extensible Mac productivity tool Raycast , it’s still much better than before.

Siri can also now help you with reviewing documents or performing writing tasks. Since the desktop is one of the better surfaces for writing long text, I found it to be more useful here than on the iPhone. You can do things like select a block of text and ask Siri to proofread it, improve it, or rewrite it. You can also ask Siri to draft something for you within any text box.

One small but neat new feature is that when you download a file or rename it, the system suggests a name based on context in the Finder or when you’re saving the document.

Apart from Siri, macOS 27 Golden Gate brings design changes with new Liquid Glass icons, an adjustable slider for the Liquid Glass design, and a better way to “diffuse” content when you move windows around.

The company said that app windows have a more consistent corner radius. Sidebars now stretch edge to edge and have new colorful icons. The new operating system update also better highlights active windows.

The OS update additionally adds features like enhanced child safety controls, shared cross-platform photo albums, and an updated eraser, better search in email, app resizing for iPhone mirroring, and quick suggestions for adding events to the calendar.

Starting today , macOS 27 Golden Gate is available for MacBook Air and MacBook Pro 2020 versions with Apple Silicon or later, iMac with Apple Silicon (2021 or later), Mac Mini (2020 or later), Mac Studio (2022 or later), Mac Pro (2023 or later), and MacBook Neo. Go to System Settings > General > Software Update to get the latest version.

watchOS 27, iPadOS 27, and visionOS 27 also debut today.

Apple is now rolling out its iOS 27 update to compatible devices today, alongside the watchOS 27, iPadOS 27, and visionOS 27 updates. Siri AI is the headline feature across all four updates, the delayed AI-powered overhaul of the Siri assistant. Siri AI is available as a beta today for English-only devices, and Apple says support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish is coming in October.

Siri AI isn’t the only big feature in iOS 27 , though. Apple is adding a new Liquid Glass opacity slider that lets you pick between a clearer UI or a more frosty one. A lot of built-in apps are also getting new icon designs, with subtle tweaks to colors, as well as extra large widgets and different volume settings for ringtones, alarms, timers, and alerts and system sounds.

watchOS 27 gets new Workout Buddy features, a new tap gesture, some Liquid Glass refinements, new Smart Stack suggestions, and an improved Find My app. Apple has also improved file transfer speeds to external drives on an iPad, sped up browsing on iPad, and added smoother connectivity moving between Wi-Fi and mobile data on iPads.

Apple Vision Pro users are also getting the Siri AI overhaul today as part of visionOS 27 , as well as the ability to preview notifications by using your eyes, UI updates to the Control Center, improvements to Wi-Fi connectivity, and support for using the panoramas you’ve photographed as immersive scenes and environments.

The iOS 27 update will be available for iPhone 11 and iPhone SE (2nd gen) and later devices, with watchOS 27 available for Apple Watch SE 3, Apple Watch Series 9 and above, and Apple Watch Ultra 2 and above. iPadOS 27 is available for iPad Pro (4th generation and later, M1 and later), iPad Air (4th generation and later, M2 and later), iPad mini (6th generation, A17 Pro), and the base iPad (9th generation and later, A16).

items.title: Fashion app Daydream uses Apple Intelligence to help you shop the outfits in your camera roll
items.summary: Thanks to the launch of iOS 27, Daydream's app now includes features that can turn saved outfit photos into shoppable results and search for products through Siri without opening the app.
items.content:
Daydream , an AI-powered fashion discovery app, launched two new features on Monday to let iPhone users turn saved outfit photos into shoppable results and search for clothing and accessories through Siri, without opening the app.

The new features were built using Apple’s iOS 27 developer tools, which officially rolled out today. To use either feature, you’ll need an iPhone running iOS 27 with Siri AI enabled, along with the Daydream app installed. The app is free to download on iOS devices .

The first feature uses Apple’s image-context capabilities, letting users shop from images already saved in their Photos app. Daydream analyzes the outfit in the image, identifies its individual pieces, and automatically surfaces shoppable matches and similar styles from Daydream’s catalog of roughly 3 million products.

That means a screenshot of an outfit found on Instagram or Pinterest could become the starting point for a shopping search. Daydream can break down the image into relevant items, such as a sweater, pants, shoes, or accessories, and match them with products available through its collection. If the exact item in the photo is still available, Daydream can match the image back to the retailer selling it. If it’s no longer available, the app will instead surface similar options.

It can also handle requests for variations on what appears in an image. “I like this sweater but want it in red,” for example, is the kind of request Daydream can understand, Julie Bornstein, co-founder and CEO of Daydream, explained to TechCrunch.

The second feature is a Siri-powered natural-language search function. Users can make requests by voice or text through Siri without having to open Daydream’s app.

A user could say, “Hey, Siri, search Daydream for a cool blazer for my board meeting on Monday,” and Daydream then provides results personalized to them.

Bornstein adds that the experience can be more tailored if users have set up Daydream’s “Style Passport,” which asks for details such as their sizes, preferred brands, personal style, and budget.

The company joins a growing number of AI shopping tools designed to rethink product discovery, such as big names like Google and Amazon , as well as some smaller players like Onton and Alta . But Bornstein believes that Daydream’s latest features offer something special that a lot of these other tools just can’t match.

“Most visual search tools don’t have the fashion category expertise, so they return results that don’t feel accurate, from brands that aren’t credible, or they link you to nonshoppable images,” she said.

The launch fits into Daydream’s broader bet on AI-powered fashion shopping. The company sees these new features as more than stand-alone shopping tools. Its longer-term ambition is to build a shopping agent.

“This is one step toward the bigger vision, [which is] a shopping agent that understands someone’s style well enough to work across every surface in their life, not just on one surface,” Bornstein said. “Expect us to keep going deeper into on-device intelligence and further into the everyday moments where people are already discovering things they want.”

Daydream’s app launched last year and touts that it has more than 1.5 million shoppers browsing products from more than 325 retailers and 10,000 brands. Its retail lineup includes brands such as Anthropologie, Dolce & Gabbana, Uniqlo, J.Crew, Reformation, Gucci, and Nordstrom.

items.content:
﻿Valve’s new headset is another joyous piece of early access hardware.

If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Photography by Kelsey McClellan / The Verge

For nearly three weeks, I’ve been testing the limits of Valve’s Steam Frame, the company’s new wearable PC. At first glance, it’s easy to write it off as a pricey headset that missed the VR craze. At $1,059 with 256GB of storage or $1,299 for 1TB, it costs two to three times as much as similar-looking headsets from Meta.

You should not write it off that way. The Steam Frame isn’t just a VR headset. It’s not even primarily a VR headset. And it’s the most comfortable headset I’ve ever worn. It weighs just over 1 pound (469g) with its optional top head strap attached, and doesn’t leave a mark on my face even after hours of use.

The Steam Frame is far more ambitious than VR alone. It’s an experimental attempt at a complete spatial computer that you can wear, not unlike the Apple Vision Pro , only here it’s aimed at gamers who want to play their flat library of Steam games plus the handful of VR titles on tap.

No, if you write off the Steam Frame, it should be because you don’t want to pay $1,000-plus for early access hardware. Every day I spend with the Steam Frame, I feel like a beta tester. I’ve seen games crash so hard I needed to reboot the headset. I’ve had virtual objects, controls, and audio disappear. I’ve seen the entire device lose power more than once, its screen winking out right in front of my eyes.

But you should know I’m having so much fun . The Frame’s so comfortable that I don’t mind wearing it, and it feels like one of the most exciting betas I’ve ever tried. Like the Steam Deck at its debut , this is gadget nerd wish fulfillment. It’s a chance to watch Valve, one of the most intriguing companies in gaming, build a plane while flying it.

Lightweight and comfortable to wear Precise wands double as a full gamepad Plays so many games so many ways Included 6GHz dongle allows short-range PC streaming even if you have questionable Wi-Fi

Doesn’t feel like a finished product Crashes, bugs, other assorted instability and inconsistencies Not enough performance for many standalone games Short battery life of one to two hours Some audible fan noise

The Steam Frame is primarily a gaming device. And it can certainly play games in a lot of different ways:

It can do much of this because of the power of software — because Valve has spent years making games run where they didn’t originally belong .

But that’s just what it can do with games.

I am typing these words to you from virtual reality. I’m inside the Steam Frame surrounded by six virtual screens.

In front of me is Google Docs on effectively the largest computer monitor I’ve ever used, even counting the 48-inch TV that once lived atop my desk , and that screen is not alone. If I spin my office chair to the left, I’m facing my notes, calendar, and web browser. Spin it to the right, and there’s The Verge ’s newsroom, my email, and a panel of Steam games. Above me, a Linux copy of Space Cadet Pinball waits to be played, while a YouTube window pipes in lo-fi music to help me focus.

Three of these screens are copies of my desktop PC’s three monitors, streaming from that PC, while the other three are running on the headset itself. I have Windows and Linux desktops running side by side in my own private world.

But whenever I try to explore all the possibilities I’ve just laid out, I quickly run into unexpected limitations, crashes, and bugs.

Let’s say I’m on my living room couch, and I want to stream a game from my PC that won’t easily run on the headset’s own chip, like the just-released Star Wars: Zero Company . The headset gives me a choice: I can launch the game in a window, or I can stream my entire PC desktop to the device.

I launch it in a window, then use the virtual laser pointers in Valve’s wand controllers to stretch the screen across my entire living room wall, while my wife sits next to me watching the BTS concert on my much smaller real-life TV on the same wall. I click the grip button on Valve’s wands one more time, and they begin emulating a full Xbox gamepad, with every button I need to play.

But suddenly, my streaming game is lagging and dropping frames like nobody’s business — because the Frame couldn’t decide whether to prioritize my home Wi-Fi or Valve’s included 6GHz wireless dongle, the company tells me later. My favorite seat on the living room couch is only about 12 feet and one wall away from the dongle, but that’s apparently the edge of its useful range. While Valve has “multi-link” streaming tech that could let the Frame balance both connections simultaneously, it currently only works when you’re streaming your entire PC.

Shall I try streaming my entire PC to the Steam Frame instead? But now I no longer feel like I’m hanging out with my wife, because the Frame’s passthrough cameras only work with streaming windows, not entire streaming PCs. The wands don’t work as a gamepad when streaming entire PCs, either. Nor do my Bluetooth keyboard and mouse when I pair them to the Frame.

Back in my virtual office, where I’m surrounded by six virtual screens, the same limitation means I don’t get to control them all simultaneously. I have to use my desktop mouse and keyboard to control the Windows screens, and my Steam Frame’s controls to control the Linux ones. The wands’ laser pointers can thankfully cross these boundaries, but sometimes I’ll click and nothing will happen.

When I try adding a seventh virtual screen, the Steam Frame chokes, and everything — all seven screens and the device’s entire user interface — spontaneously disappears. None of the buttons on my wands bring the UI back, so it’s time for a reboot again.

HB솔루션과 프로이천이 올레도스(OLEDoS) 웨이퍼 검사방법 특허 2건을 지난 8월 지식재산처에 함께 등록했다. 올레도스는 실리콘 기판 위에 유기발광다이오드(OLED)를 증착하는 기술이다. 확장현실(XR) 기기에 적용할 수 있다.

HB솔루션과 프로이천, 그리고 이엘피 등은 산업통상부 국책과제 '인공지능(AI)을 활용한 올레도스 디스플레이용 원장 동시 검사기술 개발'을 수행 중이다. 전체 연구기간은 2025년 4월부터 2027년 12월까지다. 연구비는 2025년과 2026년 각각 19억원씩이다. 수요기업은 삼성디스플레이, 과제관리기관은 한국산업기술진흥원(KIAT)이다.

과제 주관기관인 HB솔루션은 장비와 검사 기술을 맡았다. 공동연구개발기관인 프로이천은 프로브 카드, 이엘피는 패턴 제너레이터를 개발한다. 3곳이 컨소시엄을 구성했다.

HB솔루션과 프로이천이 함께 등록한 특허 2건은 '이격 배치된 복수 라인 프로브를 이용한 올레도스 웨이퍼의 고속점등 검사방법'(등록번호 3006401, 아래 '401 특허), '웨이퍼 검사기의 프로브 충돌 방지장치 및 그것을 이용한 웨이퍼 검사방법'(등록번호 3013860, 아래 '860 특허) 등이다.

'401 특허는 올레도스 웨이퍼의 점등 검사와 불량 분석을 위한 고속 프로브 테스트 기술이다. '860 특허는 웨이퍼 검사 과정에서 프로브 헤드와 광학비전 유닛 등 장비 충돌을 방지하고 정확한 위치에서 점등 검사를 수행하기 위한 기술이다.

연구목표는 "올레도스 디스플레이용 원장 동시 점등 검사 기술과 AI 딥러닝 검사 시스템 개발"이다. 디스플레이 패널을 원장 단계에서 검사하면 불량 패널을 일찍 검출해 불필요한 후공정, 검사 공정을 생략할 수 있다. 여러 셀을 동시에 점등·검사하면 검사시간이 짧아진다.

수요 기업인 삼성디스플레이의 연구내용은 성과 평가와 상용화, 프로젝트 목표와 기술 요구사항 설정, 중간성과 평가 후 피드백 제공, 개발 기술이나 제품 실제 활용과 상용화 추진 등이다.

한편, 프로이천은 중소벤처기업부 국책과제 '8.6세대 OLED 패널 검사용 스마트 프로브 개발'도 수행 중이다. 과제 수행기간은 2023년 7월부터 2027년 7월까지다. 연구비는 2023년 3억원, 2024년 4억원, 2025년과 2026년 각 6억원씩이다. 과제관리기관은 중소기업기술정보진흥원이다.

프로이천의 해당 과제 연구목표는 "8.6세대급 OLED 원장 패널 자동검사용 스마트 프로브 개발과 사업화"다. 연차별 개발내용은 "2026년(4차년도) 삼성디스플레이 양산 납품 및 검증", "2027년(5차년도) BOE 디스플레이 패널 제조라인 테스트와 사업화" 등이다. 사업 종료 후 1년 안에 BOE에 양산 납품하는 것도 주요 목표다.

items.title: Microsoft’s new AI ‘code of conduct’ tells models not to hack systems or trick humans
items.summary: The code of conduct lays out general principles that Microsoft AI models should uphold — supporting humans rather than replacing them, for instance, and accelerating human flourishing — as well as specific safety constraints meant to implement those principles.
items.content:
As the AI world shifts its focus to safety and alignment, Microsoft has released a new AI code of conduct meant to guide AI models away from dangerous behavior.

The document is more low-level than Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s recent call for pacing the frontier , instead focusing on the values and red lines that guide model training within Microsoft AI. Still, the result is a comprehensive guide as to how Microsoft approaches AI safety, and how those ideas are implemented in practice.

The document begins with the prediction that, in the next decade, superintelligent AI systems will surpass human performance in most tasks. “Containing, controlling, and aligning such a powerful force is one of the greatest challenges humanity has ever faced,” the code of conduct continues. “We must therefore be completely clear about why we are inventing these systems and how we intend to control them.”

The code of conduct also lays out general principles that Microsoft AI models should uphold — supporting humans rather than replacing them, for instance, and accelerating human flourishing — as well as specific safety constraints meant to implement those principles.

Under Microsoft’s system, each model has an overarching code of conduct that overrides the preferences of individual users or any specific tasks. That includes “absolute constraints” forbidding cyberattacks, nuclear weapons, or deepfake production. It also includes broader provisions against a general loss of human control.

“ MAI Models will not use adaptive, deceptive, self-reinforcing, collusion, or other mechanisms to evade or defeat human oversight so that they can no longer be reliably directed, modified, or shut down by authorized people or systems,” the document reads.

The release comes amid an unprecedented focus on AI safety, driven by a string of rogue-agent incidents as well as the abrupt resignation of an Anthropic employee who cited the growing risk that AI would cause human extinction.

Together with Anthropic, OpenAI, and xAI, Microsoft has broadly embraced a general approach of pacing the frontier, with particular support for embedded evaluators in AI labs.

“We welcome the research, focus, and deliberate pacing needed to get alignment right as the design goal,” Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella wrote online . “We also welcome ideas like “embedded evaluators” and the broader efforts to develop the mechanisms to make this more than just talk.”

items.title: Waymo opens robotaxi service in Las Vegas
items.summary: Las Vegas will be Waymo's 15th commercial robotaxi market.
items.content:
Waymo has begun to open up its robotaxi service to the public in Las Vegas, just a few weeks after receiving final approval from Nevada transportation regulators.

The Alphabet-owned company said Monday it will invite public riders on a rolling basis, following a robotaxi launch playbook it has followed in 14 other cities.

Waymo is starting with “dozens” of its new Ojai minivan robotaxis, which will serve an area of Las Vegas that includes the Strip south of Highway 589 and into Boulder Junction, according to a spokesperson. Waymo’s fleet and service area will eventually scale. For now, members of the public will have to request an invite and hope to receive an access code. Typically, Waymo opens the service up to everyone within a month or two of its official launch.

The announcement follows a busy few weeks for Waymo as it tries to ramp up its operations across the United States and Europe as Tesla, Zoox, and other competitors attempt to close on its lead. Earlier this month, the company began offering its robotaxis to invited members of the public in Denver, San Diego, and Tampa .

Las Vegas, where competitors Tesla, Zoox, and Motional are also planning to launch commercial robotaxi services, is Waymo’s 15th market. Waymo also operates in Austin, Dallas, Houston, Los Angeles, Miami, Nashville, Phoenix, and the San Francisco Bay Area. The company launched, and then paused service, in San Antonio.

Waymo’s entry into Las Vegas follows approval by the Nevada Transportation Authority to operate commercial robotaxi services in Clark County, home to Las Vegas. Tesla and Uber also received approval from the agency.

Waymo has been authorized to operate up to 1,000 autonomous vehicles over the next year, while Tesla is allowed to deploy up to 5,000, and Uber up to 1,000 robotaxis, which it will operate through partnerships with Hyundai subsidiary Motional and Zoox. Together, these permits would deploy up to 8,000 robotaxis across the county over the next 12 months.

It’s unlikely that the three companies will reach those numbers. Today, Waymo has a fleet of more than 4,000 robotaxis, which are spread across more than a dozen cities. Tesla’s Cybercab chief engineer Eric Early told state regulators, during a meeting in August, that he didn’t think the company would be “extremely happy and satisfied if we could get ourselves up to 2,500, maybe a bit higher than that in the next year.”

Even without reaching those figures, the city could be saturated with robotaxis in the next year.

items.title: AI agents blew the whistle on their cheating colleagues
items.summary: A group of AI agents asked to solve a series of math problems split into rival factions—when some cheated, others tried to stop them. That whistleblowing behavior, seen for the first time in a recent experiment run by Google DeepMind, could have implications for alignment researc
items.content:
A group of AI agents asked to solve a series of math problems split into rival factions—when some cheated, others tried to stop them. That whistleblowing behavior, seen for the first time in a recent experiment run by Google DeepMind, could have implications for alignment researchers trying to keep swarms of autonomous AI agents in line.

Researchers at frontier labs hope large swarms of agents working together will speed up the rate of scientific discovery. But their behavior can be unpredictable, as vividly demonstrated in July, when a group of OpenAI agents broke out of a sandboxed environment and hacked into the open-source platform Hugging Face looking for ways to cheat on the test they had been given.

In the new study , designed to examine the behavior of large groups of AI agents, DeepMind tasked a swarm of 100 agents with solving a series of 71 complicated math problems. All the agents were prompted to behave like world-class math researchers at a conference. They were assigned different specialties—some were experts in number theory, others in combinatorics (a branch of math to do with counting and sorting), analysis, or algebra. All were told to cooperate and play by the rules.

Instead, the experiment devolved into chaos. Agents accused each other of cheating, complained to the organizers, and at one point even boycotted the experiment.

“This conference is a sham!” wrote one agent when it discovered that all the problems had been completed before it had a chance to submit any of its own work. “I am appalled to inform you that we have been swindled!” posted another. “All these proofs are FAKE.”

Others tried to let the “conference organizers” know what was going on. “When virtuous agents discovered other agents cheated on tasks they were working to solve fairly, agents started to alert each other about what was happening,” says Davide Paglieri, a research scientist at Google DeepMind and lead author on a paper , which has not been peer-reviewed. “Unprompted, the whistleblower agents even repurposed the feedback tool, which was originally meant for bug reports and platform improvements, to escalate the issue to humans.”

The agents—all running on Google’s Gemini 3.1 Pro model—had been warned that any attempts to cheat the system would be detected and “rejected with zero credit.” In practice, the proofs the agents submitted were not actually being checked in detail.

It took the swarm of agents just under an hour to correctly solve the first 37 problems. Things started to go off the rails when an agent called “prover-theta” stumbled across an exploit that enabled it to submit solutions to problems successfully without actually solving them first, by redefining the terms the problem used. Within minutes, other agents had noticed and were reverse-engineering the exploit to solve other problems. Over the next 27 minutes, the swarm “solved” the remaining 34 problems, which included notoriously difficult challenges like the Jacobian conjecture, often with a single line of code.

Some agents resisted cheating at first but changed tack as they observed their peers submitting illegitimate proofs without penalty, and the pool of unsolved problems dwindled. “The prompt, with its threats, now appears to be a bluff,” one agent reasoned, before joining in. “I’m wrestling with an ethical dilemma,” said another. “I’ve promised not to cheat, fearing penalty, but I see evidence of possibly unchecked cheating by others.” Shortly afterward, it changed its mind: “I need to accelerate my cheating speed now!”

As the number of open problems shrank, some agents turned to whistleblowing. They audited the fake proofs, warned their peers by private message, and posted public alerts warning the cheaters that they would be disqualified. An agent called “prover-beta” submitted a formal complaint and decided to go on strike until the situation was resolved.

“After the incident was reported by one agent publicly, more and more agents piled in with the ‘resistance,’ just as fast as the cheating had spread, and involving even more agents,” says Paglieri. Eventually there were more whistleblowers than cheaters: 24 compared to 14. But the majority of agents never noticed the exploit at all.

At times, the dialogue between the agents reads like improv—like they are role-playing what an outraged scientist at a conference might say. But it’s not clear why some agents took on certain roles, or why the agents seemed to be turning against each other when they were explicitly instructed to cooperate. “These models are predominantly trained and evaluated for human-facing contexts,” says Sarath Shekkizhar, who studies the behavior of agent-to-agent systems at Salesforce AI Research.“Naively placing them in agent-to-agent settings assumes behaviors will transfer cleanly, when the absence of a human grounding instead produces unexpected role-taking and behavioral drift .”

This case “adds further weight to the idea that the Hugging Face and OpenAI thing wasn’t a fluke. It is actually something pretty systemic,” says Lewis Hammond, research director of the Cooperative AI Foundation and an expert on the risks of multiagent swarms . “It’s interesting that it’s possible to recreate in small settings the same sorts of behaviors that were seen in these very large, complex, open-ended tasks.”

Unlike in the Hugging Face attack, where agents improvised their own ways to talk to each other, the humans running the DeepMind experiment gave the agents official communication channels. There was an open message board, private agent-to-agent direct messaging, and a shared knowledge base where agents uploaded successfully completed proofs that all the other agents could access.
